title: Coercion of the Vulnerable
thesis: Cumulatively, more than 76,000 Canadians have died under MAID since 2016. Coercion need not involve a gun to the head: a state that offers death to the disabled but withholds housing, that offers death to veterans but delays treatment, that offers death to the chronically ill but cannot fund palliative care — that state has coerced the marginalized into a body count.

scenes.headline: Coercion of the Vulnerable
scenes.subhead: Seventy-six thousand deaths. The pattern is not random.

scenes.context: Health Canada Annual Reports on MAID, 2016 through 2024. Year-over-year growth has been double-digit since the program began. The 2024 report alone records 16,499 provisions.

scenes.speaker: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee
scenes.speaker_meta: Lessons learned — coercion and undue influence cases (2024)
scenes.quote: The Committee has reviewed cases in which the social context of the MAiD request — including pressure from family, financial inability to access alternative care, or the absence of any meaningful alternative — raised concerns about the voluntariness of the request as defined by the legislation.

scenes.speaker: Roger Foley
scenes.quote: When the only door the state opens is the one that ends my life, that is not a choice. That is coercion administered by policy.

scenes.unit: Track 2 share of all 2024 MAID deaths
scenes.context: Track 2 — the cohort whose death is NOT reasonably foreseeable — has grown every year since C-7. The C-7 framework is now exporting an increasing share of its body count to a population the 2016 statute deliberately excluded.

scenes.headline: Why this completes the doctrine
scenes.body:
The five Acts together establish the elements of Article 6 of the Rome Statute: an identifiable group, members of that group being killed (Act II), serious mental and bodily harm (Act III), conditions of life calculated to destroy (Act IV), and the intent — recorded in Hansard, in the Statutes of Canada, in Health Canada's own reports — that drives all of it (Act I).

Coercion of vulnerable groups is the closing element. It is not hypothetical. It is in the Ontario coroner's case files, in Roger Foley's evidence package to the International Criminal Court, and in the cumulative count of seventy-six thousand Canadians the Government of Canada has now killed.

Article 15 of the Rome Statute permits any person to submit information to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICC. The communications have been filed.

scenes.headline: What now
scenes.subhead: Read the evidence. File a Section 504 information. Write your MP. Forward this site.
